Q: How use Microsoft.Extensions.Logging from Library code? A:

As it is clearly explained in Logging guidance for .NET library authors:

When you need a logging object that can be passed along to multiple classes so that all of them can emit logs, use ILoggerFactory. It's recommended that each class creates logs with a separate category, named the same as the class. To do this, you need the factory to create unique ILogger<TCategoryName> objects for each class that emits logs. Common examples include public entry point APIs for a library or public constructors of types that might create helper classes internally.

TL;DR — pass ILoggerFactory and use ILoggerFactory.CreateLogger.

Q: Why can't I detach an orphan's HEAD? A:

-b/-B/--orphan indicates a named branch while --detach results in an anonymous branch, so they cannot work with each other.

For -b/-B, it's usually used in git checkout -b/-B <new-branch> <start-point>. And in git switch it's git switch -c/-C <new-branch> <start-point>. To be at a detached HEAD, you can just use git checkout/switch --detach <start-point>.

For --orphan, it creates an unborn branch before you run git commit. So, after git commit, you can use git checkout/switch --detach HEAD. For git checkout, --detach can be omitted.
